analysis.title: Ferrari Q3 Review: A Clear Road Ahead
key_insights: UBS Sales and Trading commentary (not UBS Research) on Ferrari's Q3 2026 results, dated 4-Nov-2026. UBS research rating is Buy, price target US$450 unchanged.

Ferrari's order book now reaches into 2028 and Luce is fully allocated for 2027. UBS reads this as support for durable growth (UBSe cars and spare parts +9% organic sales growth) while keeping exclusivity.

Personalisation is above 21% of cars and spare parts revenue versus a medium-term target of about 19%. Management expects it to continue in Q4. Visibility beyond Q4 is limited because customers finalise choices three to four months before delivery.
Part of the ASP strength comes from elevated personalisation on special models, which are concentrated this year and likely to normalise.
UBS expects sales growth at more than 2x the pace of the broader Luxury sector in 2026E and 2027E, and EBITDA margin of 39.5% in FY27 with a path to at least 40% by 2030.
UBS says Ferrari's premium to luxury peers is above historical levels, but P/E is still below its long-term average and Luxury-sector valuations are near cyclical lows.
Q3 revenue was €1,896m, 1% below consensus (+2% vs UBSe). EBITDA was €753m, 1% above consensus (+3% vs UBSe). EBITDA margin was 39.7% vs consensus 39.0% (UBSe 39.3%).
Q3 organic sales growth was +10% (consensus +9%, UBSe +8%). Cars and spare parts organic growth was +10% with volumes -1% and price/mix +11% (consensus +9%, UBSe +7%).

Ferrari raised FY26 guidance: sales about €7.65bn, adjusted EBITDA at least €3.0bn, EBITDA margin at least 39.2%, industrial FCF up to €1,650m. Drivers were stronger personalisation, lower currency headwinds net of hedges, and second place in the Formula 1 championship.
EBITDA guidance is in line with consensus. UBS attributes the initial negative share reaction to expectations and positioning, not fundamentals, and calls any weakness a buying opportunity.
Management expects H2 ASP slightly above H1 and shipments to return to year-on-year growth in Q4 on easier comparatives and wider distribution of the new range.
F80 deliveries were about 50 units in the quarter, a deliberately gradual ramp. Luce production is under way with first deliveries expected in Q4 and international media test drives in Q1 2027.
FX headwind is now expected at €150-200m versus about €200m previously. 2027 FX is hedged at about 70% on a 12-month rolling policy.
Residual values are very healthy across models and regions, and in some areas customers prefer hybrids over ICE.

market_movers.rationale: UBS reiterates Buy after Q3 beat on organic growth and margin plus a raised FY26 guide. Earnings upgrades of up to 2% are offset by USD strength, so the target is unchanged.

sector_views.rationale: UBS expects Ferrari sales growth at more than 2x the Luxury sector pace while sector valuations sit near cyclical lows. This is a view on Ferrari relative to the sector, not an explicit sector rating.

earnings_insights: Ferrari Q3 2026 reported 11/4: revenue €1,896m vs consensus €1,906m (UBSe €1,854m), a small miss against consensus.
Q3 2026 reported adjusted EBITDA €753m, about 1% above consensus and 3% above UBSe. EBITDA margin 39.7% vs consensus 39.0% (UBSe 39.3%). EBIT margin 29.7% vs consensus and UBSe 29.5%.

Q3 2026 organic sales +10% vs consensus +9% (UBSe +8%). Cars and spare parts +10%, volumes -1%, price/mix +11% vs consensus +9% (UBSe +7%). Sponsorship, commercial and brand +7% (consensus +6%, UBSe +4%). Other +17% (consensus +21%, UBSe +18%).

FY26 guidance raised (company, 11/4): sales about €7.65bn (prior about €7.6bn, consensus €7.64bn, UBSe €7.60bn), adjusted EBITDA at least €3.0bn (prior at least €2.97bn, consensus €3.00bn, UBSe €2.98bn), EBITDA margin at least 39.2% (prior at least 39.0%), industrial FCF up to €1,650m (prior at least €1,550m, consensus €1,615m, UBSe €1,583m).

Valuation per UBS: RACE on 19.7x 2027e and 18.5x 2028e EV/EBITDA in one section, 19.3x and 18.0x in another, and 20.5x FY26e and 18.5x FY27e in a third. The note is internally inconsistent. 3-year sales and EBITDA CAGR (2026-29e) of +8% and +9%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Management's updated estimate, down from about €200m, helped by a more favourable USD spot rate.

trade_ideas.description: Buy $RACE on post-results weakness, UBS price target US$450
trade_ideas.rationale: Order-book commentary is reassuring and EBITDA margin progression is encouraging.

risk_factors: Visibility on personalisation beyond Q4 is limited.
Special-model personalisation is concentrated this year and likely to normalise.
USD strength offsets earnings upgrades in the price target.
Ferrari's premium to luxury peers is elevated versus historical levels.
Q3 volumes were -1% and F80 ramp is gradual.
vol_and_positioning: UBS says the initial negative share reaction reflects positioning and expectations, since some investors wanted more from the guidance range.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS says order book into 2028, Luce sold out for 2027, personalisation above 21% and a raised guide support durable growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Shares reacted negatively as EBITDA guidance of at least €3.0bn only matched consensus and revenue was 1% below consensus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Personalisation normalising below the elevated level or shipments failing to return to year-on-year growth in Q4.

theme_stances.key_argument: Order book into 2028 and Luce allocated for 2027 reinforce the durability of Ferrari's growth.
theme_stances.evidence: order book reaching into 2028 and Luce fully covered for 2027
